questionText:
Consider a demand paging system with four page frames (initially empty) and LRU page replacement policy. For the following page reference string

$$7, 2, 7, 3, 2, 5, 3, 4, 6, 7, 7, 1, 5, 6, 1$$

the page fault rate, defined as the ratio of number of page faults to the number of memory accesses (rounded off to one decimal place) is ________.
explanation:
Step-by-step trace of LRU Page Replacement (4 frames):

Total Memory Accesses = 15

1. 7: [7] — Page Fault (1)
2. 2: [7, 2] — Page Fault (2)
3. 7: [7, 2] — Hit
4. 3: [7, 2, 3] — Page Fault (3)
5. 2: [7, 2, 3] — Hit
6. 5: [7, 2, 3, 5] — Page Fault (4)
7. 3: [7, 2, 3, 5] — Hit
8. 4: Replaces 7 $\rightarrow$ [4, 2, 3, 5] — Page Fault (5)
9. 6: Replaces 2 $\rightarrow$ [4, 6, 3, 5] — Page Fault (6)
10. 7: Replaces 5 $\rightarrow$ [4, 6, 3, 7] — Page Fault (7)
11. 7: [4, 6, 3, 7] — Hit
12. 1: Replaces 3 $\rightarrow$ [4, 6, 1, 7] — Page Fault (8)
13. 5: Replaces 4 $\rightarrow$ [5, 6, 1, 7] — Page Fault (9)
14. 6: [5, 6, 1, 7] — Hit
15. 1: [5, 6, 1, 7] — Hit

Total Page Faults = 9

$$\text{Page Fault Rate} = \frac{\text{Total Page Faults}}{\text{Total Memory Accesses}} = \frac{9}{15} = 0.6$$
